content.value_statement: Newsletter operators need a clear way to compare subscriptions, sponsorships, and growth investments. This skill creates labeled revenue models, rate cards, and disclosure checks from the data you provide.
actual_capabilities: Creates paid-tier revenue models using stated conversion and price assumptions.
Builds CPM, click-priced, or flat-fee sponsorship rate cards.
Projects revenue at list-growth milestones using explicit growth-loop inputs.
Labels model inputs and outputs as Measured, User-provided, or Estimated.
Flags missing sponsorship disclosures and unsupported offer claims.
Produces a handoff summary for ROI or email-quality review.
limitations: Does not calculate final ROI, payback, or list value.
Does not access email platforms, analytics tools, or ad networks directly.
Does not supply benchmark conversion rates, CPMs, or subscriber counts.
Does not determine legal compliance or approve marketing claims.

use_cases.title: Price a paid newsletter
use_cases.description: Model tiers, conversion assumptions, and recurring revenue before launching a paid offer.

use_cases.title: Create a sponsor rate card
use_cases.description: Set sellable inventory, rate basis, fill assumptions, and floor prices for sponsorships.

use_cases.title: Compare growth paths
use_cases.description: Compare subscription-only and hybrid revenue plans at specific audience-growth milestones.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic model
prompt_templates.prompt: Model paid subscriptions for my newsletter. I have 5,000 active subscribers, a 40% open rate, and a $10 monthly tier.

prompt_templates.title: Build a sponsor rate card
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sponsorship rate card for my 20,000-subscriber newsletter. It has a 45% open rate, weekly sends, and two sponsor slots.

prompt_templates.title: Compare revenue mixes
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare paid-subscription-only and hybrid subscription plus sponsorship plans for a 45,000-subscriber list. Use my 42% open rate, 3.1% click rate, and stated prices.

prompt_templates.title: Plan growth and compliance
prompt_templates.prompt: Project newsletter revenue at current size, 25% growth, and 50% growth. Include referral assumptions, sponsorship disclosures, and claims that need review.

output_examples.input: A 20,000-subscriber weekly newsletter with a 40% open rate and one primary sponsor slot.
output: Sellable impressions per send: 8,000, labeled Measured.
Primary sponsorship price: requires a stated CPM or flat-price assumption.
Open loop: confirm sponsor disclosure wording before sale.

output_examples.input: A 5,000-subscriber newsletter with a $10 monthly paid tier and a 3% conversion assumption.
output: Assumption: conversion rate is Estimated and must be validated.

best_practices: Provide active-subscriber counts, engagement metrics, cadence, and current prices.
State every conversion, fill-rate, CPM, and growth assumption explicitly.
Label sponsorships and route unsupported claims for review before publishing.
anti_patterns: Do not present estimated revenue as measured performance.
Do not use subscriber lists without confirming commercial-mail consent.
Do not invent benchmarks when data is missing; mark the value as needing a source.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide active-subscriber count, open and click rates, send cadence, revenue goal, and any prices or targets.

faq.question: Can it create a sponsor rate card?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure CPM, click-priced, or flat-fee inventory with explicit assumptions.

faq.question: Can it estimate subscription revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. It applies your stated price and conversion assumption and labels the result as estimated.

faq.question: Does it connect to my email platform?
faq.answer: No. It uses numbers you provide from your own exports or reports.

faq.question: Does it calculate ROI?
faq.answer: No. It prepares revenue inputs and recommends a separate ROI calculation step.

faq.question: Does it provide legal approval?
faq.answer: No. It flags disclosure and claim issues for appropriate review.
